newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Wheat Pool asks for wheat meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sask Wheat Pool asks for wheat meeting.

text.p: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool, Canada's largest grain handling firm, said on Tuesday it asked Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale to "call an emergency meeting" on delayed wheat shipments to Pacific ports.

SWP's board of directors "asked the Minister of Agriculture to call an emergency meeting to address the very serious grain transportation problem that currently exists on the Prairies," the Wheat Pool said in a prepared statement.
Demurrage fines levied by importers of Canadian spring wheat since railway shipment delays began early in January now exceed C$15 million, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
More than 1.5 million tonnes of grain shipments are now backlogged because of the slow pace of shipment to Pacific ports, the CWB said.
"While the target for grain car unloads at the west coast is 4,900 unloads per week, since December 1, actual unloads have been well below target," the SWP statement said.
"In some weeks unloads have been less than half of what was planned," it said. Forty-two ships waited to load Feb 10.
The grain cooperative said it was "optimistic" Goodale would call a meeting within the "next few days."
Canadian National Railway Co spokesman Jim Feeny said his firm's delivery performance on grain to Pacific ports continued to improve this week but declined to provide specific details.
Officials at Canadian Pacific unit CP Rail System were not immediately available for comment.
Rail rates on grain cannot exceed a federally mandated cap while other commodities may be getting priority over grain due to premiums payments, transportation industry analysts said.
The Canadian government is due to review the grain rail rate cap and perhaps its necessity in 1999.
Goodale was in federal Parliament for Question Period and not available for comment.
